decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard display very close to the core offer, it is cheap to keep available and still preserves upside for customer-specific demand.
The pegboard-backed cardboard display is adjacent to the established range and likely worth retaining because the option value remains positive while carrying costs are low.
This standard quarter-pallet cardboard display appears most replaceable within a crowded set of similar variants, so by now the firm has likely learned enough to prune it.
The eighth-pallet format broadens the firm's core display portfolio with limited additional commitment, so it remains a reasonable option to hold open.
The wooden display pallet is less aligned with the firm's cardboard-centered capabilities and likely costs more complexity to maintain, reducing its option value after several years.

A media-specific quarter-pallet display is a narrower niche than the firm's general display solutions, and after several years the firm would likely reallocate resources if demand has not clearly scaled.
